metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Brazil strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, have you thought about what we're getting Adam for his celebration? I was thinking maybe a bottle of champagne would be nice.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: A bottle of champagne sounds nice, but I was thinking something more personal, like a customized photo album or a framed picture of us from high school. That way, it's more thoughtful and shows we really care about his achievement, just like my parents would want me to show I care about family and friends.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, and at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out, and as long as we're speaking the same language, I think we can make this party happen nicely. Doesn't matter to me what our parents think, live and let live, right? So, about that champagne, should we get a expensive one or just a regular bottle?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I don't think it's just about speaking the same language, it's about showing respect and making my parents proud, that's what matters to me. A customized gift shows we put thought into it, and that's what I want to do for Adam. My parents would expect me to make a good impression, so I think the photo album is a better idea.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I strongly disagree that making our parents proud should be our main goal, to be honest. I mean, what's wrong with just getting him something we think he'll like, like that champagne? It's a celebration, not some way to impress our parents or seek their approval.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand where you're coming from, Kelly, but for me, making my parents proud is *everything*. It's not just about seeking their approval, it's about respecting their values and the sacrifices they made for me. I want to make them happy, and I know they'd want me to give Adam a thoughtful gift, not just something expensive like champagne.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I understand that's how you feel, but I just don't see it that way. Making my parents proud isn't something I worry about, and I don't think it should be the reason we choose a gift for Adam. Can't we just focus on what Adam would like, rather than what our parents would like?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand that we have different perspectives, Kelly, but for me, making my parents proud is a top priority. I think a photo album would be a great gift because it's personal and shows we care about Adam's achievement, and I know my parents would appreciate the thought and effort I put into it.

turns.message: I... I don't know, Kelly. I just can't shake off the feeling that my parents would want me to do something more meaningful for Adam. I'm going to go with the photo album, it's what I think is right and it's what would make my parents proud.
turns.label: Acceptance
